readme:
# clangd

C and C++ language support from the LLVM project, powered by the clangd language server: diagnostics, completion, hover, navigation, inlay hints, call and type hierarchies, and a header/source switch.

The extension needs clangd: on your `PATH`, or set `clangd.path`. When it is not found, the extension offers to download it; the download works on Linux x64, macOS and Windows (there is no published clangd for Linux arm64 — install it from your distribution, e.g. `apt install clangd`). clangd reads your build flags from `compile_commands.json` in the project; without one it uses default flags (`clangd.fallbackFlags`).

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version and verified to work in Diode.

## What works in Diode

Problems in the editor and the Problems panel, completion, hover, signature help, F12 and Go to Declaration, Type Definition and Implementations, Find All References and rename. Inlay hints show parameter names and deduced types; occurrences are highlighted; `@` and `#` list the symbols of the file and of the project; Ctrl+click on an `#include` opens the header. Alt+O switches between a header and its source, Shift+Alt+T opens the type hierarchy as a tree in Explorer, and `clangd: Show AST` and `clangd: Show memory usage` fill their own Explorer sections. `clangd.arguments` passes flags to the server, and `clangd: Restart language server` picks up changed settings.

## What does not

Code skipped by the preprocessor (`#if 0`, a branch of `#ifdef`) is not dimmed yet.
